_comment: Worked example: register a LOCAL DEV Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app in the developer console and capture its client id/secret.
Built from a real hand-driven agent-browser session (comet profile, CDP 127.0.0.1:9222, --session comet).
Keys starting with '_' are ignored by pixel (not part of the Flow schema); they are documentation for humans.
HOW TO RUN
pixel flow save atlassian-oauth-app --from-file crates/pixel-flow/examples/atlassian-oauth-app.json
pixel flow run atlassian-oauth-app --var accept_terms=true [--var app_name='My Local Dev App'] [--var callback_url=http://localhost:3000/oauth/atlassian/callback]
OAUTH_ENV_OUT=./.env.oauth crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture atlassian
OAUTH_CALLBACK_URL=<the callback_url you used> OAUTH_ENV_OUT=./.env.oauth crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py check atlassian
TERMS: accept_terms defaults to false. Only accept_terms=true ticks 'I agree to be bound by Atlassian's developer terms'.
Without it the flow stops after the form (Create stays disabled, nothing is created).
WHY THE LAST TWO COMMANDS ARE NOT FLOW STEPS: pixel-flow cannot write files, read env vars or call curl, and `pixel flow run`
discards `eval` output. oauth-env.py reads the secret straight from the page into $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600) and prints only lengths.
LOGIN IS OUT OF SCOPE. The comet session must already be signed in. A login or 'Verify it's you' page makes the flow STOP on
purpose (a `click` whose ref_hint can never match). It never types credentials. Sign in by hand, then re-run.
SCOPES are vars: --var atlassian_jira_scopes=a,b  --var atlassian_confluence_scopes=c,d (comma-separated scope codes; defaults
read:jira-work,read:jira-user and read:confluence-content.all). The flow ticks each code on the Jira / Confluence API scope pages. Only those two
APIs are added; to add another API, copy the Add / Configure / Edit Scopes / tick / Save step group. Callback URL is set under Authorization > OAuth 2.0 (3LO).
NOT IDEMPOTENT: every run creates a NEW app. Delete stale local-dev apps by hand in the console.
AFTER THE FLOW (manual follow-up): your backend/app reads OAUTH_ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_SECRET from its
process environment. `source` the env file written to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT before starting the API. Never commit that file.
NEVER put real client ids or secrets in this file.
name: atlassian-oauth-app
title: Register a local-dev Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app and capture client id/secret
description: Creates an Atlassian developer-console OAuth 2.0 integration (default name 'My Local Dev App', Resource-level access), adds Jira API + Confluence API with the scopes from atlassian_jira_scopes / atlassian_confluence_scopes (defaults: 2 Jira + 1 Confluence read scopes), adds the 3LO callback URL, and ends on the Settings page. Follow with `oauth-env.py capture atlassian` to write OAUTH_ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_ID / OAUTH_ATLASSIAN_CLIENT_SECRET to $OAUTH_ENV_OUT (mode 600), then `oauth-env.py check atlassian`. Terms checkbox is gated behind --var accept_terms=true (default false). Login is out of scope; the flow stops if signed out. Not idempotent.
preconditions: Verify comet-cdp is up (port 9222) and `agent-browser --session comet tab list` answers
The comet browser profile is ALREADY signed in to developer.atlassian.com (this flow never types credentials)
Read Atlassian's developer terms yourself; pass --var accept_terms=true only if you accept them (default false: the flow stops before creating anything)
Export OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> before the capture step (the file receives secrets: keep it out of git, mode 600 is enforced)

vars.name: homepage_url
vars.description: Accepted for a uniform interface with the other oauth-app flows; the Atlassian creation form has no homepage field, so it is unused

vars.name: callback_url
vars.description: 3LO callback URL your local app's OAuth callback route listens on

vars.name: atlassian_jira_scopes
vars.description: Comma-separated Jira API scope codes to tick (changeable). Page JS repeats this default for an omitted var

vars.name: atlassian_confluence_scopes
vars.description: Comma-separated Confluence API scope codes to tick (changeable). Page JS repeats this default for an omitted var

vars.name: accept_terms
vars.description: 'true' ticks the Atlassian developer-terms checkbox on your behalf. Anything else (including omitted) leaves it unticked and the flow stops before creating the app. Must be passed with --var; it has no effective default

steps.rationale: Open the developer console app list. Already-authenticated profile expected; Atlassian redirects to a login page when signed out.
steps.on_failure: If the open times out, re-run `agent-browser --session comet tab list` and retry once

steps.rationale: The console is a slow SPA; let the app list (or a login redirect) render
Login is out of scope. Signed-out or re-verify ('Verify it's you') pages stop the flow; never type credentials.
steps.condition: page shows 'Log in to continue' or 'Verify it' or 'Enter your email'

then.rationale: STOP: not signed in to Atlassian (or a re-verification prompt is showing). Sign in by hand in Comet, then re-run this flow. (Fails on purpose: the ref_hint can never match, so the flow aborts with this message.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - Atlassian login or Verify-its-you required in the comet session - a human must sign in, then re-run the flow

steps.rationale: Capture the app list page; the header has a 'Create' menu button
Open the Create menu
Choose 'OAuth 2.0 integration' (not 'Forge app' or 'Connect app')
Let the creation form render
Capture the form: Name textbox, Access type checkbox(es), developer-terms checkbox, Create button (disabled)

PITFALL (append): the Name box may be PREFILLED and a real 'type' APPENDS to it, so use `fill` (replaces), then verify the value below. PITFALL (events): a value set from page JS does not fire real input events and leaves Create disabled; agent-browser `fill` does fire them.
Re-snapshot so the Name textbox shows its current value
Verify the Name value took. NOTE: {{app_name}} only substitutes when passed with --var; with the default this check reads as not met and the fallback below re-enters the name, which is harmless.

otherwise.rationale: Select all existing text so the typed name REPLACES it (macOS shortcut; use Control+a elsewhere)
Real key typing (fires real input events) over the selected text

steps.rationale: REQUIRED 'Access type': choose 'Resource-level'. Create stays disabled until name, access type AND the developer-terms checkbox are all set.
steps.on_failure: Re-snapshot; the option may be a radio or a labelled row. Pick 'Resource-level' only.

steps.rationale: TERMS GATE: tick 'I agree to be bound by Atlassian's developer terms' ONLY when --var accept_terms=true was passed. Unset or any other value leaves it unchecked and Create disabled (fail-closed: {{accept_terms}} is not defaulted, so an omitted var stays a literal and never equals 'true'). By passing accept_terms=true the human accepts the terms.
Verify Name, Access type and terms state before Create
Click the form's Create (the LAST 'Create' button inside the dialog/form: the header 'Create' menu button must not be hit). Reports DISABLED instead of clicking when the form is incomplete.
steps.value: (()=>{const root=document.querySelector('[role=dialog],form')||document;const bs=[...root.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b=>b.innerText.trim()==='Create');const b=bs[bs.length-1];if(!b)return 'create-button-not-found';if(b.disabled||b.getAttribute('aria-disabled')==='true')return 'create-DISABLED (name, access type or terms incomplete)';b.click();return 'create-clicked'})()

steps.rationale: App creation redirects to /console/myapps/<uuid>/overview
Still on the creation form means Create did not fire: terms not accepted (accept_terms != true) or the form is incomplete. Stop.
steps.condition: page shows 'I agree to be bound'

then.rationale: STOP: the creation form is still open. Either accept_terms was not true (re-run with --var accept_terms=true after reading Atlassian's developer terms) or a required field is missing. Nothing was created. (Fails on purpose.)
then.ref_hint: STOP - Atlassian app was not created - accept_terms must be true and name and access type must be set

steps.rationale: Confirm the app overview page (/console/myapps/<uuid>/overview) is showing
Open the Permissions section in the app sidebar
Let the API list render
Add 'Jira API'. Row-scoped DOM click because every row has an identical 'Add' button, so a text match on 'Add' alone is ambiguous.
steps.value: (()=>{const lab='Add',want='Jira API',other='Confluence API';const b=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(x=>x.innerText.trim()===lab).find(x=>{let n=x.parentElement;for(let i=0;n&&i<8;i++,n=n.parentElement){const t=n.innerText||'';if(other&&t.includes(other))return false;if(t.includes(want))return true}return false});return b?(b.click(),'clicked '+lab+' in row '+want):'not-found '+lab+' in row '+want})()

steps.rationale: Let the row flip from 'Add' to 'Configure'
PITFALL: refs shift after each Add. Re-snapshot between the two clicks.
Add 'Confluence API' (same row-scoped approach)
steps.value: (()=>{const lab='Add',want='Confluence API',other='Jira API';const b=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(x=>x.innerText.trim()===lab).find(x=>{let n=x.parentElement;for(let i=0;n&&i<8;i++,n=n.parentElement){const t=n.innerText||'';if(other&&t.includes(other))return false;if(t.includes(want))return true}return false});return b?(b.click(),'clicked '+lab+' in row '+want):'not-found '+lab+' in row '+want})()

steps.rationale: Let the row flip from 'Add' to 'Configure'
Both APIs should now show 'Configure'
Configure Jira API (row-scoped: both rows have 'Configure')
steps.value: (()=>{const lab='Configure',want='Jira API',other='Confluence API';const b=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(x=>x.innerText.trim()===lab).find(x=>{let n=x.parentElement;for(let i=0;n&&i<8;i++,n=n.parentElement){const t=n.innerText||'';if(other&&t.includes(other))return false;if(t.includes(want))return true}return false});return b?(b.click(),'clicked '+lab+' in row '+want):'not-found '+lab+' in row '+want})()

steps.rationale: Navigates to the Jira API configuration page
Open the scope editor
Let the scope table render

PITFALL: scope checkboxes have NO labels. Map each wanted scope code to the checkbox in the SAME table row via the DOM (leaf element whose text equals the code; the nearest ancestor holding exactly one checkbox). Throws if any wanted scope was not ticked, so a wrong row cannot be saved silently. Scope list comes from --var atlassian_jira_scopes (comma-separated, default read:jira-work,read:jira-user).
steps.value: (()=>{const raw='{{atlassian_jira_scopes}}';const want=(raw.startsWith('{{')?'read:jira-work,read:jira-user':raw).split(',').map(x=>x.trim()).filter(Boolean);const out={};for(const code of want){const cell=[...document.querySelectorAll('*')].find(e=>e.children.length===0&&e.textContent.trim()===code);let n=cell,cb=null;while(n&&!cb){const l=n.querySelectorAll?n.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]'):[];if(l.length===1)cb=l[0];else if(l.length>1)break;n=n.parentElement}if(cb&&!cb.checked)cb.click();out[code]=!!(cb&&cb.checked)}if(!want.length||Object.values(out).some(v=>!v))throw new Error('scope-tick-failed '+JSON.stringify(out));return JSON.stringify(out)})()
steps.on_failure: Re-snapshot, find each scope's row by its code text and tick its checkbox by hand-written eval; do not tick by position.

steps.rationale: Verify every Jira scope in atlassian_jira_scopes is ticked before saving
Save the Jira scopes
Let the save settle
Back to the Permissions list
Let the API list render
Configure Confluence API (row-scoped)
steps.value: (()=>{const lab='Configure',want='Confluence API',other='Jira API';const b=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(x=>x.innerText.trim()===lab).find(x=>{let n=x.parentElement;for(let i=0;n&&i<8;i++,n=n.parentElement){const t=n.innerText||'';if(other&&t.includes(other))return false;if(t.includes(want))return true}return false});return b?(b.click(),'clicked '+lab+' in row '+want):'not-found '+lab+' in row '+want})()

steps.rationale: Navigates to the Confluence API configuration page
Open the scope editor
Let the scope table render

Tick the Confluence scopes (same unlabeled-checkbox mapping) from --var atlassian_confluence_scopes (comma-separated, default read:confluence-content.all). Exact text match, so '.all' never ticks '.summary'.
steps.value: (()=>{const raw='{{atlassian_confluence_scopes}}';const want=(raw.startsWith('{{')?'read:confluence-content.all':raw).split(',').map(x=>x.trim()).filter(Boolean);const out={};for(const code of want){const cell=[...document.querySelectorAll('*')].find(e=>e.children.length===0&&e.textContent.trim()===code);let n=cell,cb=null;while(n&&!cb){const l=n.querySelectorAll?n.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]'):[];if(l.length===1)cb=l[0];else if(l.length>1)break;n=n.parentElement}if(cb&&!cb.checked)cb.click();out[code]=!!(cb&&cb.checked)}if(!want.length||Object.values(out).some(v=>!v))throw new Error('scope-tick-failed '+JSON.stringify(out));return JSON.stringify(out)})()
steps.on_failure: Re-snapshot, find each scope's row by its code text and tick its checkbox by hand-written eval; do not tick by position.

steps.rationale: Verify every Confluence scope in atlassian_confluence_scopes is ticked before saving
Save the Confluence scopes
Let the save settle
Back to the Permissions list
Let the list render
CHECK: the Permissions page should now report as many scopes in use as the two scope vars list in total (default 3). If not, stop and fix by hand.
Open the Authorization section
Let the authorization types render
Add 'OAuth 2.0 (3LO)' (row-scoped Add; the page may list other authorization types)
steps.value: (()=>{const lab='Add',want='OAuth 2.0 (3LO)',other=null;const b=[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(x=>x.innerText.trim()===lab).find(x=>{let n=x.parentElement;for(let i=0;n&&i<8;i++,n=n.parentElement){const t=n.innerText||'';if(other&&t.includes(other))return false;if(t.includes(want))return true}return false});return b?(b.click(),'clicked '+lab+' in row '+want):'not-found '+lab+' in row '+want})()

steps.rationale: Let the Callback URLs field render
Capture the 3LO configuration with the 'Callback URLs' textbox
PITFALL: REAL key typing is required here. `fill` leaves 'Save changes' disabled because the form never sees real input events.
Verify the callback URL is in the box and 'Save changes' is enabled
Save the callback URL
Let the save settle
Open the Settings page, which shows the Client ID and Secret
Let the settings render

FLOW ENDS HERE on /console/myapps/<uuid>/settings. 'Client ID' is a textbox value; 'Secret' is a MASKED password input whose .value holds the real secret (never read it from the snapshot). NEXT: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> crates/pixel-flow/examples/oauth-env.py capture atlassian   then   ... check atlassian

success_signal: page text contains 'Client ID' and 'Secret'. Then run: OAUTH_ENV_OUT=<path> oauth-env.py capture atlassian && oauth-env.py check atlassian (a bogus code must NOT come back invalid_client)
